4.9. Upgrading Across the Units Change#

This page is for people who already run SUEWS (Surface Urban Energy and Water Balance Scheme) through SuPy and need to know what changes when they move to forcing contract 2.1.0 and output contract 2.0.0. It covers forcing files, saved output and code that reads saved output. YAML configuration files are converted separately; see Transitioning to YAML-based Configuration.

The principle behind the change is “plain numbers inside, units at the edges”. The model still computes in its own units. Units are now declared, checked and converted only where data enters SuPy (forcing files) and where it leaves (saved output), and every unit string follows the CF (UDUNITS-2) notation of supy.units.

4.9.1. Summary#

Forcing files that declare nothing load exactly as before. You only need to act if you pass a units= declaration, or if your forcing carries observed soil moisture.

Saved water fluxes change unit and meaning. Written precipitation, irrigation, evaporation, runoff, drainage, water-use, storage-change and snow water fluxes are now interval-mean rates in kg m-2 s-1, not amounts in mm per output interval. Any script that reads these columns from saved text or Parquet output must be updated.

Everything else keeps its values. Other variables are written with the same values; some unit strings are respelt in CF notation, and every saved file now carries its units beside it.

The breaking changes are:

  • written water fluxes are interval-mean rates in kg m-2 s-1 (Water fluxes in saved output);

  • a units= declaration for rain or water use must include a time unit (Declared rain and water-use units need a time unit);

  • observed soil moisture is supplied as sm in kg m-2 instead of xsmd (Forcing contract versions).

4.9.2. Forcing#

4.9.2.1. Declaring the units of a forcing file#

Forcing files are normally written in the units of the forcing registry, which Forcing variable reference lists. A file in other units can now be loaded by declaring its units in Python. The declaration is a mapping from column name to unit string, passed as units= to SUEWSSimulation, update_config(), update_forcing() (file inputs), from_file(), read_forcing() or load_forcing_grid(). It is a Python argument applied to that load only; it is not a YAML field, and the YAML schema is unchanged.

Declared columns are converted to the registry units when the file is read, before validation, timestamp construction and resampling. Missing-value sentinels (-999) and NaN are kept as missing. Columns that are not declared are read exactly as before.

Before, a file holding temperature in kelvin and pressure in hPa had to be rewritten in degrees Celsius and kPa before loading. After:

from supy import SUEWSSimulation

sim = SUEWSSimulation("site.yml", units={"Tair": "K", "pres": "hPa"})

In-memory forcing (a DataFrame passed to update_forcing()) is already in runtime units and refuses a declaration.

4.9.2.2. Declared rain and water-use units need a time unit#

A declaration for rain, the bulk water use Wuh, or any of the seven per-surface water-use columns (wuh_paved to wuh_water) must be a rate: a mass flux such as kg m-2 s-1 or a depth rate such as mm h-1 or mm d-1. SuPy converts the declared rate to the amount per forcing interval that the model uses, from the interval of the file’s timestamps. A bare amount (mm, m, kg m-2) is refused, because it does not say over what time the water fell.

This only affects code that passes units=; files without a declaration keep their per-interval amounts in mm and load bit for bit as before.

Before (refused from forcing contract 2.1.0):

sim = SUEWSSimulation("site.yml", units={"rain": "mm"})

ValueError: forcing column 'rain': water flux requires a time unit: use kg m-2 s-1, mm h-1 or mm d-1

After, for a file of hourly rainfall rates:

sim = SUEWSSimulation("site.yml", units={"rain": "mm h-1"})

If the file holds the amount that fell in each row’s interval, as SUEWS forcing files traditionally do, leave rain out of the declaration; it is then read as before.

4.9.2.3. Errors when loading a declaration#

Every error names the column it concerns. The causes and fixes are:

  • unknown column in units declaration: the key is not a forcing column or file alias; check the spelling against Forcing variable reference (names are case-insensitive).

  • declared column is absent from file: the file has no such column; remove the key or load the right file.

  • duplicate units declaration: the same column is declared twice, for example under a name and its file alias; keep one.

  • unit must be a string or a message that the unit is not in the SUEWS unit vocabulary: write the unit as a CF string accepted by parse_unit(), such as "degC", "hPa" or "mm h-1".

  • cannot convert ... the dimensions differ: the declared unit measures a different quantity from the column (for example "K" for pressure).

  • time coordinates (iy, id, it, imin) take no units declaration: the timestamp columns are integers, not physical quantities; remove the key.

  • water flux requires a time unit: see the section above.

4.9.2.4. Forcing contract versions#

The forcing contract moves from 1.2.0 to 2.1.0 in two steps.

  • 2.0.0 replaces observed xsmd with sm at the same column position: the instantaneous liquid-water content of a specified soil layer in kg m-2, from which SuPy derives the moisture deficit. This needs matching YAML changes (soil_moisture, the observation layer and soil_field_capacity); see Upgrading to Schema 2026.6.dev9 for the YAML upgrade and the “Observed liquid soil water” section of Meteorological Forcing Data for the forcing. An xsmd column that is entirely missing, as in most existing files, is still read as missing sm for modelled soil moisture, with a FutureWarning; this allowance ends at forcing contract 3.0.0. Observed runs, and any xsmd column carrying values, are refused.

  • 2.1.0 records the rate unit that a rain or water-use declaration is converted to, as described above. The file layout and the units of undeclared files do not change.

4.9.2.5. Converting observed soil moisture#

A configuration with observed soil moisture (legacy method 1, volumetric, or 2, gravimetric) cannot be upgraded on its own: the YAML and its xsmd forcing are converted together, in one step that writes a new YAML, a new forcing file and a JSON manifest, and never changes the inputs.

  1. Add soil_field_capacity to the YAML. Every non-water land-cover surface with a positive fraction needs land_cover.<surface>.soil_field_capacity, the volumetric liquid-water content at field capacity in m3 m-3, such that \(1000\,\theta_{fc}\,d \ge C\), with \(d\) the surface’s soil_depth in metres and \(C\) its soil_store_capacity in kg m-2. The legacy schema has no such field and the converter does not invent one; when it is missing or too small, the converter names each surface and the smallest value that satisfies the inequality. Take the value from soil data for the site.

  2. Fill gaps in the observed series. The converter checks every row of the forcing file it is given, whatever the run’s start_time and end_time: a missing value (-999 or NaN) anywhere in xsmd is refused, with the first missing timestamp in the message. Earlier releases filled such gaps silently. Either fill them in the legacy xsmd column before conversion, for example by interpolating in time with pandas, and record how they were filled; or trim the forcing file to a period with complete observations and set the run’s start and end inside it. Shortening the run alone does not help, because conversion still reads the whole file. A run of the converted case also refuses missing sm within its period.

  3. Convert, first with --dry-run:

    suews convert -i config.yml -o new/config.yml \
    --forcing forcing.txt --forcing-output new/forcing.txt \
    --manifest new/conversion.json \
    --layer-top 0 --layer-depth 0.35 --dry-run

    --layer-depth is the represented soil layer in metres and must equal soil_depth (in mm) of every contributing surface; --layer-top is 0. The legacy depth is treated as the sensor installation depth and replaced by --layer-depth (recorded in the manifest changes) unless --legacy-depth-is-thickness confirms that it was the layer thickness. With the ambiguous observed selector add --source-unit 'm3 m-3' or --source-unit 'kg kg-1'; for a forcing file without a header row add --source-contract (1.0.0, 1.1.0 or 1.2.0). Repeat without --dry-run to write the files.

  4. Run inside the observed period. Observed sm is interpolated to the model time step only between valid observations and is never extrapolated, unlike the other forcing variables. With hourly forcing whose first row is 01:00, a run starting at 00:00 has no sm for its first steps and is refused; start it at or after the first observation.

4.9.3. Saved output#

4.9.3.1. Water fluxes in saved output#

Saved text and Parquet output now writes every water flux as the mean rate over the written interval, in kg m-2 s-1: the water accumulated in the interval divided by the seconds it covers. Previously these columns held the amount in mm accumulated over the interval, so an hourly Rain of 0.5 mm is now written as about 1.389e-4 kg m-2 s-1. Text output writes these columns in scientific notation so that light rain does not round to zero.

The change covers 71 variables:

  • SUEWS group: Rain, Irr, Evap, RO, TotCh, SurfCh, Drainage, FlowCh, AddWater, ROSoil, ROPipe, ROImp, ROVeg, ROWater, WUInt, WUEveTr, WUDecTr, WUGrass, MeltWater, SnowCh, SnowRPaved and SnowRBldgs;

  • snow group: the per-surface Mw_*, RainSn_* and frMelt_* columns;

  • debug group: the per-surface wu_*, ev0_*, ev_* and drain_* columns.

Water stores, deficits and snow water equivalent (for example SMD and the State columns) stay amounts; their unit is now spelt kg m-2 instead of mm, with unchanged values, because 1 kg m-2 of liquid water is 1 mm.

Since 1 kg m-2 is 1 mm, the amount per written interval is the rate multiplied by the interval in seconds. Before, an hourly text file gave the rainfall per hour directly:

import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("Kc1_2012_SUEWS_60.txt", sep=r"\s+")
rain_mm = df["Rain"]  # mm in each hour

After:

rain_mm = df["Rain"] * 3600  # kg m-2 s-1 times 3600 s gives mm per hour

Alternatively, ask for a depth rate when saving, so the file holds mm per hour directly:

output = sim.run()
output.save("output", units={"Rain": "mm h-1"})

A water flux can be requested in any rate unit (mm h-1, mm d-1, kg m-2 s-1), but not as an amount: units={"Rain": "mm"} raises an error naming the variable. The written interval of each column is recorded in the metadata described below, so code reading the files does not need to assume it.

4.9.3.2. Output held in memory#

The output returned by run() is not converted: output.df holds the model’s native amounts, so Rain is still mm per model timestep. output.units reports the unit of the values actually held, which can therefore differ from the catalogue unit of the saved files. Convert in memory with to_units():

output = sim.run()
output.units[("SUEWS", "Rain")]                  # "mm" (per model timestep)
hourly = output.resample("h")                    # mm per hour, summed
rates = hourly.to_units({"Rain": "mm h-1"})      # mm h-1, interval mean

to_units accepts only rate units for water fluxes, so output.to_units({"Rain": "mm"}) is refused even though output.units reports mm: mm there names the amount in each held row, whose interval changes with resampling, while a requested unit must be a quantity that stays the same whatever the rows’ interval. Use resample to change the interval of the amounts, and to_units with mm h-1 or mm d-1 for rates.

When resampled, accumulated water now sums: MeltWater, the frMelt_* refreezing amounts and the debug wu_*, ev0_*, ev_* and drain_* columns were previously averaged, so their resampled values change.

4.9.3.3. Requesting other units#

Any output variable with a unit can be converted after the run, for example heat fluxes to kW m-2 or temperatures to kelvin. Conversion happens once, outside the model, through convert():

converted = output.to_units({"QE": "kW m-2", "T2": "K"})
output.save("output", units={"QE": "kW m-2", "T2": "K"})

The same units= mapping is accepted by save() and save(). A name that occurs in more than one group needs a (group, variable) key. On-scale temperatures convert with their offset, while temperature differences (marked temperature: difference) convert by scale only. Output already streamed to disk with output.stream_chunk cannot be converted afterwards; request units on output held in memory. See Output Files for details.

4.9.3.4. DailyState water totals#

DailyState P_day and the daily water-use totals WU_EveTr1-3, WU_DecTr1-3 and WU_Grass1-3 stay daily totals in mm, written with the same values as before; on the first day of a run that starts part-way through a day they are the totals of the model steps that day actually covers. A day’s row is written at its last model step, so a run that ends part-way through a day writes no DailyState row for that day. They are not converted to rates: they accept amount units (mm, m, kg m-2) and refuse rate units with daily water totals require amount units. Their metadata now says time: sum with the interval covered day, and the number of seconds each day covers is recorded as information (daily_coverage_s in text sidecars); it never rescales the totals. When resampled over several days, these totals are now summed instead of taking the last day’s value:

monthly = output.resample("ME")
monthly.df[("DailyState", "P_day")]  # monthly total in mm

4.9.3.5. Resampling to calendar periods and partial intervals#

Output can be resampled to calendar frequencies such as "W", "MS", "ME" and "YE" as well as fixed ones. Each bin keeps track of the seconds it actually covers: a trailing partial bin is kept for every variable (a run ending at 01:15 has an hourly row at 02:00), and a water rate in a partial or calendar bin is divided by the seconds covered, not by the nominal length of the bin. Resampling a rate again weights each source bin by its coverage, and a sum over a bin with no data is missing rather than zero.

Every group, DailyState included, is binned and labelled with the same closed="right", label="right" rule at both fixed and calendar frequencies, so one row holds one period across all groups: output.resample("D") labels day D’s Rain and DailyState P_day alike at D+1 00:00, and output.resample("ME") puts January’s Rain and January’s DailyState P_day in the row labelled 2012-01-31, with the step stamped 2012-02-01 00:00 counting towards January (see Timestamp Convention).

Output resampled to a fixed frequency (for example output.resample("D")) is saved at that interval, and its files and metadata say so, with one exception: DailyState rows resampled to more than one day (for example output.resample("2D")) cannot be saved, because the files describe each DailyState row as one day; save groups=["SUEWS"], or the native or daily output, instead. Calendar-resampled output cannot be saved to files, because a calendar period has no fixed interval to name the files and describe the rows; the error begins Calendar-resampled output (for example ME or W) cannot be saved to files. Save the native output, or write monthly.df with pandas.

4.9.3.6. Units and cell methods beside saved output#

Saved output now describes itself, so readers no longer need to assume units or intervals:

  • each text file <file> gets a sidecar <file>.units.json holding output_contract_version and, for every column, units, cell_methods, description, interval and, where it applies, units_metadata; DailyState sidecars also hold daily_coverage_s. Text file contents are otherwise unchanged. The save methods return the data files and the run’s checkpoint JSON (and, from save(), provenance.json), but not the .units.json sidecars, which sit beside the files they describe;

  • Parquet output carries the same per-column fields as Arrow field metadata and output_contract_version in the schema metadata, and keeps the written units and coverage when read back with pandas.read_parquet;

  • output.units maps each column to its unit, and output.units.metadata gives the full record.

cell_methods follows CF Conventions and names the written interval, for example time: mean (interval: 1 hour) for a water rate saved hourly and time: point for an instantaneous value. Columns outside the output registry are marked status: unknown and given no unit.

Before, a reader had to know the units of each column from the documentation. After:

import json

meta = json.load(open("Kc1_2012_SUEWS_60.txt.units.json", encoding="utf-8"))
meta["output_contract_version"]           # "2.0.0"
meta["columns"]["Rain"]["units"]          # "kg m-2 s-1"
meta["columns"]["Rain"]["cell_methods"]   # "time: mean (interval: 1 hour)"

Parquet output saved after an in-memory run (output.save(format="parquet")) is deprecated and warns with a FutureWarning; stream Parquet output with model.control.output.stream_chunk instead (see Parquet Format Output). Both paths write the metadata above.

4.9.3.7. Output contract 2.0.0#

The output contract moves from 1.1.8 to 2.0.0 through 1.1.9.

  • 1.1.9 writes every unit in CF notation (for example W m-2, kg m-2 for water stores, 1 for ratios) and adds cell_methods and units_metadata to every catalogue entry. Values, names, groups and layouts are unchanged.

  • 2.0.0 is a major release because written water fluxes change from amounts to interval-mean rates, as described above.

The written contract version is recorded in every sidecar and Parquet file, so code that reads output from several SuPy versions can branch on it. The contract history is described in Data-interface versioning.
